To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) RNA seq is a powerful tool for transcriptome profiling; (b) RNA seq data can be analyzed using a variety of tools, but there are some important considerations to take into account; (c) we present a computational and statistical workflow for RNA seq differential expression that is based on DESeq and edge R; and (d) the workflow is implemented in the free open source software R and Bioconduction.

the DESeq and edge R methods for differential expression analysis of high-throughput RNA sequencing data are highly comparable, and that both methods are robust to a range of experimental and data processing choices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development, evaluation, and dissemination of computational and statistical methods for the analysis of high throughput sequencing data.
the development and application of computational and statistical methods for RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) analysis, and the development of tools to support these methods.
the development and implementation of computational and statistical approaches to RNA seq data analysis, and in particular, differential expression analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this protocol provides a state-of-the art computational and statistical workflow for RNA seq differential expression analyses.
this protocol provides a robust, flexible, and easy to use workflow for the analysis of RNA seq data.
the protocol described here can be applied to a broad range of experimental designs, and is likely to provide the most accurate differential expression analysis results available today.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this protocol provides a state of the practice computational and statistical RNA sequencing differential expression analysis workflow.
we present a state of the-art RNA seq analysis pipeline that is easy to set up, flexible, and that can be easily extended and adapted for new experiments.

we have provided a detailed description of a computational pipeline that can help researchers in performing RNA seq differential expression analyses, and we have made available a set of R scripts that can be easily used to perform the described analyses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while there are many options for RNA seq data analysis, there are some clear best practices that can be followed to ensure high-quality results.
the choice of statistical test for differential expression analysis is not as crucial as the choice of appropriate quality control checks and normalization.
the use of appropriate tools can greatly reduce the risk of spurious conclusions.
